subject: English
topic: Odd Sentence Out — Paragraph Coherence (Set W7)

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three form a coherent paragraph on a topic. Identify the sentence that does NOT belong.
A: Reading improves vocabulary and strengthens language skills.
B: Regular exercise helps maintain a healthy weight and boosts energy.
C: Books expose readers to diverse perspectives and ideas.
D: Reading before bedtime is often recommended to improve sleep quality.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Sentences A, C, and D all discuss benefits of reading. Sentence B shifts topic to physical exercise — entirely unrelated to the paragraph's theme. The odd sentence is B.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three form a coherent paragraph about the internet and communication. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: The internet has revolutionised the way people communicate globally.
B: Social media platforms allow instant sharing of news and events.
C: The first steam engine was invented during the Industrial Revolution.
D: Video conferencing has made remote work a more viable option for millions.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A, B, and D discuss the internet's role in modern communication. Sentence C refers to the Industrial Revolution and steam engines — it belongs to a completely different historical and technological context. The odd sentence is C.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three are about the Mughal Empire in India. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: The Suez Canal, connecting the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, was completed in 1869.
B: Akbar's policy of Sulh-e-Kul promoted universal religious tolerance across the empire.
C: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
D: Aurangzeb expanded Mughal territory to its greatest geographical extent.
questions.explanation: A is correct. B, C, and D all relate to Mughal emperors (Akbar, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb) and the Mughal Empire. Sentence A is about the Suez Canal, a 19th-century Egyptian engineering project — completely unrelated. The odd sentence is A.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three form a coherent paragraph about India's banking system. Identify the sentence that does NOT belong.
A: Commercial banks accept deposits and provide loans to individuals and businesses.
B: The Reserve Bank of India serves as the central bank and monetary authority.
C: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles to Mexico each winter.
D: NBFCs (Non-Banking Financial Companies) provide financial services without a banking licence.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A, B, and D all discuss India's banking and financial system (commercial banks, RBI, NBFCs). Sentence C is about monarch butterfly migration — a zoology fact entirely out of context. The odd sentence is C.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three form a coherent paragraph about water conservation. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: Rainwater harvesting is an effective method to conserve and reuse water.
B: Drip irrigation can reduce water usage in farming by up to 60%.
C: Smartphones have fundamentally transformed how people consume digital content.
D: Treating wastewater and recycling it can significantly reduce freshwater demand.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A, B, and D discuss water conservation techniques (rainwater harvesting, drip irrigation, wastewater treatment). Sentence C is about smartphones and digital content consumption — a completely different topic. The odd sentence is C.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three discuss ancient Indian civilisations. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: The Indus Valley Civilisation had advanced urban planning with sophisticated drainage systems.
B: Artists of the Italian Renaissance transformed European art by mastering perspective.
C: The Vedic period saw the composition of the four Vedas in the Sanskrit language.
D: Harappan cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa had standardised brick sizes across sites.
questions.explanation: B is correct. A, C, and D all refer to ancient Indian civilisations (Indus Valley, Vedic period, Harappan cities). Sentence B refers to the Italian Renaissance, a European cultural movement that began in the 14th century — unrelated to ancient India. The odd sentence is B.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three are about Gandhi's independence movement. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: Garuda, the eagle deity, is the national emblem of Indonesia and appears on its coat of arms.
B: The Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920 saw millions refuse to cooperate with British administration.
C: Gandhi's Salt March in 1930 was a direct challenge to the British salt monopoly in India.
D: The Quit India Movement of 1942 called for immediate end to British colonial rule in India.
questions.explanation: A is correct. B, C, and D all relate to Gandhi's independence movement in India (Non-Cooperation, Salt March, Quit India). Sentence A is about the Garuda symbol of Indonesia — a completely unrelated mythology/heraldry fact. The odd sentence is A.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three form a coherent paragraph about nutrition and health. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin upon exposure to ultraviolet sunlight.
B: Iron deficiency leads to anaemia, characterised by persistent fatigue and weakness.
C: Omega-3 fatty acids found in fish oil are known to benefit cardiovascular health.
D: The invention of Gutenberg's printing press revolutionised the spread of knowledge in Europe.
questions.explanation: D is correct. A, B, and C all discuss nutritional science (Vitamin D, iron, omega-3 fatty acids). Sentence D is about Gutenberg's printing press in medieval Europe — a history of technology fact, completely outside the nutrition context. The odd sentence is D.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three discuss yoga and meditation. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: Yoga has its roots in ancient Indian philosophy, including the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali.
B: Regular meditation reduces cortisol levels and significantly lowers psychological stress.
C: Pranayama techniques involve controlled breathing exercises that improve lung capacity.
D: The discovery of penicillin by Alexander Fleming transformed the treatment of bacterial infections.
questions.explanation: D is correct. A (yoga origins), B (meditation reducing cortisol), and C (pranayama breathing) all belong to the yoga and meditation theme. Sentence D — about Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin — is a medical history fact with no connection to yoga. The odd sentence is D.

questions.stem:
Four sentences are given below. Three are about wildlife conservation in India. Identify the odd sentence out.
A: Project Tiger, launched in 1973, helped reverse the decline of Bengal tigers in India.
B: The rhinoceros population has shown significant recovery in Kaziranga National Park.
C: India's pharmaceutical industry is the world's largest producer of generic medicines.
D: The global ban on ivory trade has contributed to stabilising elephant populations.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A (Project Tiger), B (rhino recovery in Kaziranga), and D (ivory ban stabilising elephant populations) are all about wildlife conservation. Sentence C — about India's pharmaceutical industry being the largest generic drug producer — belongs to a completely different industrial/economic context. The odd sentence is C.
